record.title: Runtime admission substitutes zero for authoritative policy usage
record.description: In a supported act-mode configuration, a submitter holding a still-valid signed Blessing issued before usage limits were reached can potentially execute a restart after recorded diagnosis-loop or Project daily-spend limits require denial. Runtime admission supplies zero for those quantities instead of obtaining current recorded usage, while the canonical policy gate applies both limits to runtime actions. Correct HMAC, an allowed human approver, target allowlisting, safe scale bounds and the local runtime action count remain required. The affected boundary is the admission owner's current policy decision under the actuator's Docker or Kubernetes authority. The shared helper is used by both the active local SQLite path and the optional API claim path. No runtime acceptance or backend effect was observed.
record.claimed_root_cause: claims.runtimeDecision reconstructs SharedPolicyContext with diagnosisLoops: 0 and llmSpentTodayUsd: 0 for every request. These are authoritative state facts, not known-zero properties of a runtime operation. ContextSchema cannot carry them, AdmissionRules has no usage reader, and neither SQLite admission nor API ActionRepo resolves the recorded Project/incident usage before calling this helper. PolicyContextService and AuditRepo already demonstrate the authoritative values and fail-closed handling elsewhere, but runtime admission bypasses that dependency.

trace.description: The request holder submits an unconsumed signed runtime action whose approval interval still includes the delivery time.
Strict parsing and HMAC verification authenticate the action, approval and available context. The signed context has no authoritative usage counters.
The active store obtains its clock and per-service action count and calls admissionDecision. It has no dependency that reads recorded diagnosis-loop or daily-spend usage.
The helper passes zero diagnosisLoops and zero llmSpentTodayUsd into the canonical policy engine, irrespective of the real recorded state.
This gate denies runtime actions when either actual usage quantity reaches its configured limit, but the substituted zeros pass positive limits when the other checks pass.
A require_approval decision from the incomplete facts becomes no denial reason, allowing the valid human approval to satisfy admission.
The token/action claim is committed under the incomplete policy decision and reported as claimed.
The late check covers approval eligibility and breaker state only; it does not fetch usage or restore the omitted policy gate inputs before run is invoked.

For a valid Docker restart action, the privileged backend sends the container restart request even though a policy decision with the recorded usage would require denial. This final result remains to be demonstrated with a recording stub.

evidence.description: The shared policy contract requires complete facts and explicitly states that missing counters are never inferred.

Runtime decision supplies actionsLast10Min from admission but hardcodes diagnosisLoops and llmSpentTodayUsd to zero. openPrsLastHour is also zero, but it is not used by the runtime-specific PR/action branch and is not part of this claim.
Diagnosis-loop and daily-spend limits are unconditional gate terms after the runtime-versus-PR rate-count choice. They therefore apply to runtime actions.
The strict signed context permits only category, signals and confidence, so even an honest request producer cannot provide these omitted facts through the current wire contract.
The production local admission path obtains only the per-service runtime action count before invoking the shared runtime decision.

The optional API claim path calls the same runtimeDecision helper after counting action claims; it does not resolve Project/incident policy usage either. This is a source-visible sibling variant of the same root cause.
The authoritative context path reads recorded usage for the granted Project, service and incident and includes it in SharedPolicyContext instead of assuming zero.
Recorded usage derives daily Project model spend and per-incident diagnosis-call counts. Parsing rejects unknown or invalid costs, establishing that unavailable usage must not silently become zero.
The post-claim eligibility recheck covers breaker and approval checks only, so there is no later authoritative-usage check that prevents the proposed effect.
The active launcher constructs DurableAdmission with policy, clock, audit, mode and breaker dependencies; no recorded-usage source is attached.

blockers: The decisive bounded comparison and backend-stub observation were not executed. Complete OS-enforced memory and cumulative disk sandbox controls are unavailable, and the assignment forbids executing project code or tests. All evidence is source-only with no retained artifact.

validation_plan.local: Within a parent-approved OS sandbox, use dummy Project 101, incident and service records, a dummy HMAC key, an act-mode policy with positive diagnosis and spend limits, a fixed clock, scratch-only SQLite admission and recording runtime backends. Obtain policy context from dummy authoritative collaborators showing diagnosisLoops equal to its limit, then separately llmSpentTodayUsd equal to its limit, after the signed approval was issued but before it expires. Confirm decide with each full recorded context denies. Deliver the otherwise valid signed request through createActionHandler and establish whether admission still returns executed and records one stub backend invocation. Repeat the shared-helper comparison for API admission with dummy storage only if needed to validate that variant. Stop at the wrong decision or stub invocation; use no real provider, container, broker, credential or shared database.
